reviewType: independent test-oracle mathematics and scope review
scope: Finite convex face membership and camera-based boundary visibility
Independence from production data-hidden/style and renderer caches
Hidden/visible/helper stroke acceptance and negative controls
No production or authored lesson changes
mathematicalFindings: Newell normals are oriented away from the body center; the world camera direction matches the orthographic depth direction. A boundary segment is hidden only when both endpoints belong to at least one finite supporting face and all such faces are back-facing.

Coplanarity plus consistent edge-cross-product signs is valid for the planar convex polygons used here. An independent scan verified planarity, convexity and convex-solid containment for every face of all 186 authored models.

Checking all supporting faces handles silhouette edges. A reverse winding does not change visibility. Infinite plane extensions are excluded by finite polygon membership. Flat projection and helper roles retain their explicit display contract.

additionalBoundaryControls: shared edge with two back-facing adjacent faces is hidden
shared edge with front/back adjacency is visible

limitations: No fresh native Chromium/layout execution was performed by this reviewer. Final browser CI remains required.

This is a finite boundary-face visibility oracle, not a general-purpose interior-segment ray-occlusion rule. Existing interior constructions ii-self-9 B1-D, ii-self-7 O-T and ii-self-8 P-Q retain the current solid-line convention; 12 unsupported segment/camera occurrences were excluded from the independent boundary-ray comparison.

The independent ray comparison used all 186 authored cards in initial/intermediate/final states at the default and two additional cameras, not arbitrary nonconvex models or every possible floating-point tangent camera.
notes: The six mutation controls reject wrong dash styles for hidden/visible/helper lines and wrong hidden flags for each role. No golden baseline was changed and no production hidden flag was used as expected output.
The full saved-artifact reanalysis was performed separately by /root/geometry_release_review; it is not represented here as a new browser run.
